title: Fastify Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Return a greeting
entries.summary: A Fastify handler can return a value directly. Open GET /.
notes: Return the result or send it with reply; do not do both.

entries.name: Return an object
entries.summary: Fastify turns a returned object into JSON. Open GET /book.
notes: Return data, not a hand-built JSON string, when possible.

entries.name: Read a route input
entries.summary: A colon marks a path parameter. GET /hello/Ravi puts the name in request.params.
notes: Path values are text unless a schema converts and validates them.

entries.name: Read a query string
entries.summary: Query input follows the question mark. GET /search?q=cat reads q.
notes: Check query values rather than assuming they are always strings.

entries.name: Read a JSON body
entries.summary: Fastify can parse JSON bodies. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}.
notes: Content-Type tells the server how to read the body.

entries.name: Validate a path value
entries.summary: A schema describes allowed data. GET /books/3 converts and checks id as a positive integer.
notes: Schemas must describe the input shape you actually expect.

entries.name: Run a step before a handler
entries.summary: A preHandler hook runs before the route handler. GET / uses the request field set by the hook.
notes: Use async hooks or callback hooks consistently; do not mix both styles.

entries.name: Share a helper
entries.summary: decorate adds a named helper to the Fastify instance. GET / uses that helper.
notes: Register the helper before the route uses it.

entries.name: Group routes in a plugin
entries.summary: register gives a plugin its own scope. A prefix puts its routes under /api. Open GET /api/books.
notes: The plugin prefix is part of the final URL.

entries.name: Choose response fields
entries.summary: A response schema can choose which fields are sent. GET /book keeps title and leaves out internalNote.
notes: A response schema is not a replacement for deciding which data is safe to return.

entries.name: Give a clear error reply
entries.summary: setErrorHandler handles errors from routes. GET /broken returns a simple public message.
notes: Avoid showing private stack traces to clients.

entries.name: Test without an open port
entries.summary: inject runs a request inside Fastify. This example prints the response body and closes the app without listening.
notes: Close the app after tests so resources are released.
